source_identity: The containing commit identifies the tested tree. The candidate changes dev-noisemaker/pixel-parity.html (adds the rotate_animated_uniform_parameter case; no existing case replaced), scripts/test.mjs (expectPass 63), scripts/ci-gate.mjs (TOTAL_CASES 63), test/ci-gate-accounting.test.mjs (denominator 63), docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, docs/COMPLETION_GAPS.md, and this receipt. Port source (src/) is unchanged; no bundle rebuild is required or performed.
purpose: Attribute the long-standing Linux host residual on rotate_animated_parameter (96/16384 bytes, max delta 1) to a precise mechanism using controlled probes, and add a matched-path sweep case that demonstrates byte-exact animated-parameter parity on this host.

probes.method: Temporary probe page (deleted after the run): render legacy Hydra gradient(0).rotate(30, 0) at time 0.25; render the port DSL gradient(speed: 0).rotate(angle: osc(min: 0.2, max: 0.4, speed: 1), speed: 0) at time 0.25; render the port DSL with a constant angle 30; compare all three; dump the fused pipeline's uniform bindings and intercept WebGLRenderingContext/WebGL2RenderingContext uniform1f during the animated render.
results: animated (DSL osc angle) vs legacy rotate(30, 0): 96/16384 bytes differ, max delta 1 (the documented residual, reproduced).
port constant angle 30 vs legacy rotate(30, 0): 0/16384 bytes differ (exact).
port constant angle 30 vs port animated: 96/16384 bytes differ, max delta 1.
Uniform bindings dumped: angle = Oscillator{oscType 0 (sine), min 0.2, max 0.4, speed 1, offset 0} with uniformSpecs {min: 0, max: 100}; speed = 0.

uniform1f interception during the animated render: exactly one value near 30 uploaded: [30] with Math.fround(v) === Math.fround(30). The engine evaluates the DSL oscillator to the float32 value 30 at time 0.25 and uploads exactly 30.

Probing port constants 30 +/- k*2^-22 (k in -2..2, the float32 neighborhood of 30) against the animated render: every constant differs from the animated render by 96/16384 bytes, max delta 1 - i.e. no float32 angle value reproduces the animated output, so the difference is not the uploaded angle value.
probes.conclusion: The port and legacy receive the identical uniform angle (30.0f). The 96-byte delta is produced by the shader path difference: legacy Hydra inlines constant numeric arguments into the generated GLSL (its generator emits `ang = 30.0 + 0.0 * time`), so SwiftShader constant-folds cos/sin at shader compile time, while the port's fused shader (and any animated legacy chain) reads the angle from a uniform and computes cos/sin at runtime. SwiftShader's runtime trig of the uniform differs from its compile-time folded trig by 1 ulp on some pixels.

probes.method: Temporary probe page (deleted after the run): render legacy Hydra gradient(0).rotate(() => 30, 0) at time 0.25 (a JS function argument, so legacy Hydra itself drives the angle through a per-frame uniform instead of inlining a constant) and compare against (a) the port animated render and (b) legacy's own constant-argument render rotate(30, 0).
results: legacy function-argument angle (uniform path) vs port animated (uniform path): 0/16384 bytes differ - byte-exact on this Linux SwiftShader host.

legacy function-argument angle vs legacy constant-argument rotate(30, 0) - both renders produced by legacy Hydra alone on the same host: 96/16384 bytes differ, max delta 1 - the identical residual signature.
probes.conclusion: The residual reproduces inside legacy Hydra itself between its inlined-constant and uniform shader paths. It is a SwiftShader compile-time-constant-folding vs runtime-trig precision artifact, not a port translation or engine-evaluation difference: the port's animated-parameter path is byte-exact against legacy's animated-parameter path on this host.

documented_residual.name: rotate_animated_parameter
documented_residual.attribution: Legacy Hydra inlines the constant angle argument into its generated GLSL while the port's animated DSL path uses a uniform; SwiftShader computes runtime cos/sin of the uniform 1 ulp differently from its compile-time folded constant. The same 96/16384, max-delta-1 signature appears between legacy Hydra's own function-argument and constant-argument renders on this host (P2), and the port's animated path is byte-exact against legacy's animated path (0/16384).
